transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-03
Time: 15:00 UTC (45 minutes)
Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM) - Emberfield: Priya (CTO), Rajiv (Head of ML), Mark (Infra), Aisha (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check + discuss adding EU region and failover/burst capacity for APAC pilot. Agreement in principle to extend 12 months + top-up reserved capacity after benchmark. Security docs requested.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity uplift, geo failover, VPC/KMS, perf benchmarking, pricing options

Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript:
00:00 Lena (Redwood AE): alright everyone thanks for making the time, quick intro — i'm lena, i'll run through agenda. Jordan's our solutions engineer, maya on CSM side. hows everyone doing?
00:12 Priya (CTO): good, thanks. busy quarter but this is important.
00:18 Lena: great. main goals: renewal conversation, talk about adding eu region and a failover plan for asia pilot, and agree next steps on benchmarks and docs.
00:30 Rajiv (Head of ML): i want to make sure the latency numbers you showed last quarter hold when we move some traffic to eu and when we enable the apac pilot. also cost per token is going to be a big driver for us.
00:44 Jordan (Redwood SE): absolutely. quick call out — we tested the same model at 1.2k seq earlier and saw median p50 latency around 120ms on dedicated, with batching optimizations. for eu we typically recommend the eu-west cluster (dedicated), or private vpc for dna sensitive workloads.
01:05 Mark (Infra): when you say dedicated do you mean reserved gpu pools? curious about burst behavior.
01:12 Jordan: yes reserved GPU pools + burst capacity. autoscaling policy will hold baseline and allow bursts up to 2x for short windows. note there is a tradeoff: burst uses shared capacity and is billed differently.
01:25 Priya: okay. can you do a failover plan if primary eu region has an outage? we need cross-region routing and a cold standby in us-east maybe.
01:36 Jordan: yup, smart routing supports policy-based failover. you can set primary->eu, fallback->us-east, with model variant mapping if certain quantized variants are used in fallback. the routing decision is per-request so session affinity with kv cache can be tricky — we can replicate the kv cache to standby but there's a cold-warm behavior.
02:00 Rajiv: replication for kv cache — that could add complexity and cost. can you spell out the consistency model?
02:08 Jordan: it's eventual; we replicate prefixes and warm caches when possible. in practice we recommend prefix caching for the majority of session state and accept small cache-warmup latency on failover. we can surface cache hit metrics in the console so you can tune TTLs.
02:28 Priya: security wise, we need details on KMS integrations and audit logs. we're subject to health-data regs in two countries.
02:36 Lena: we'll share our SOC2 + security pack. for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and for hosted we support key wrapping. audit logs include per-request traces and token-level usage.
02:50 Aisha (Procurement): what's the data retention and purge policy? our legal team will want to know.
02:55 Maya (CSM): retention is configurable per-account; default is 90 days for logs, you can request shorter retention and we can do on-prem install if needed. we'll include the retention matrix in the docs we send.
03:12 Mark: on networking, any special peering? we want to avoid public egress for PHI traffic.
03:18 Jordan: VPC peering or private link is supported. for private deployment we'll run control plane in your VPC or offer a private control plane model. there's an option to keep inference nodes entirely inside customer network for onprem setups.
03:33 Rajiv: good. pricing — we want options: reserved baseline + burst, and maybe a smaller dedicated cluster in eu plus pay-as-you-go hosted fallback. can you map that to cost estimates?
03:45 Lena: yes. typical structure: reserved capacity monthly commit (discounted), burst on top (at higher rate), and hosted fallback (per-token). we'll produce a few scenario tables with exact numbers based on your qps and model mix.
04:00 Priya: timeline — procurement would like renewal signed by end of feb to align with vendor review windows. we can commit if benchmarks look good.
04:10 Lena: understood. planning to run a 2-hour perf benchmark where we run 4 representative models (conversation model, summarization, embedding batch, and a long-form generation) to validate latency, throughput, and cost. Jordan — can we do that the week of feb 9?
04:22 Jordan: yes that'll work. we'll need their sample traffic and auth to spin up a dedicated test cluster. mark, you'll provide traffic profile?
04:29 Mark: yes, i'll extract qps, p95 seq length and peak windows and share. expect it by feb 6.
04:35 Jordan: perfect. we'll also run the same tests with and without kv cache warmup to show delta.
04:42 Priya: one more thing — we have an internal preference to limit vendor lock. can you outline rollback and exportability of user data and model traces?
04:50 Lena: we offer data export APIs and can provide sanitized usage logs. for private deployments you keep full control; for hosted we have contractual export guarantees in the enterprise addendum. we'll include that language in the security pack.
05:05 Aisha: procurement asks if there's any competitor pricing intel we should be aware of?
05:12 Lena: generally AtlasAI does lower headline costs but with less mature failover and less tooling for batching/cost telemetry; CloudServe has strong region presence in APAC but their private deployment path is more heavyweight. we'll outline differences briefly in the follow-up.
05:30 Rajiv: technical question — quantization: do you support int8 or nf4 for our models? we want to preserve quality.
05:38 Jordan: yes, runtime supports nf4 and int8 paths; we recommend nf4 for conversational models to preserve fp quality. we'll include model-specific regression numbers from our lab.
05:52 Priya: ok. what are the options for canary deployments and rollbacks? we need safe rollouts for model updates.
05:58 Jordan: canary via traffic split in the control plane. you can do percentage rollouts, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. we can wire that into your CI to trigger rollouts.
06:12 Mark: any limit on concurrent kv sessions? we've seen token spikes during billing windows.
06:18 Jordan: we size kv cache per cluster; reserved pools give you predictable cache capacity. we can also configure eviction policies to prioritize active sessions.
06:30 Priya: what's the expected uplift in throughput when we move from hosted to dedicated for our profile?
06:36 Jordan: typical uplift 2-3x throughput with lower p95 latency for large batch workloads due to dedicated gpu scheduling and optimized kernels. exact numbers will be in the benchmark.
06:50 Rajiv: can we test private today or is that a longer lead time?
06:55 Lena: private deployments have longer lead time, usually 6-8 weeks for onprem packaging and security review, shorter for VPC-based private control plane. for your timeline we can start with dedicated eu pool and plan private as next quarter.
07:12 Priya: that seems fine. procurement note — contract amendment for adding geo region, is that a simple addendum?
07:18 Lena: yes, we draft an amendment that adds regional nodes and reserved capacity line items; nothing major unless you need additional compliance language.
07:26 Aisha: do you offer a trial uplift for free or do we need to pay for benchmark hours?
07:30 Lena: we typically include a small amount of pilot credits and charge for extended dedicated test clusters; we'll flag what's covered in the pricing doc.
07:40 Mark: what telemetry will we get during benchmarks — token-level, per-route latency?
07:44 Jordan: token-level cost, per-request latency breakdown, per-model breakdown and cache hit rates. we'll share a spreadsheet with the same fields.
07:55 Priya: okay good. on the EU specifics — data residency — we need to keep all PII within EU borders. can you guarantee that for the eu dedicated cluster?
08:06 Jordan: yes, eu dedicated cluster keeps inference and logs in the eu cluster. for backups and control plane interactions we can configure to avoid cross-border egress. we'll detail that in the sovereignty section of the docs.
08:20 Rajiv: any caveats on model variants? if fallback uses smaller quantized variant will we see quality drift?
08:27 Jordan: some drift is expected; our routing policies allow variant mapping with configurable thresholds so you can prefer quality over cost or vice versa. the console will flag expected quality deltas.
08:40 Priya: let's talk next steps and owners — we want the pricing and security docs by feb 5, benchmark week feb 9, mark to provide traffic feb 6. is that aligned?
08:50 Lena: yes, that's what we'll do. Jordan will run benchmarks and ship results, lena will update the quote, maya will coordinate CSM onboarding.
09:00 Aisha: procurement will review the amendment draft once received. goal to sign before feb 28.
09:06 Lena: perfect. any last questions?
09:12 Mark: just one — support SLAs during failover, what uptime and latency guarantees apply?
09:18 Jordan: SLA covers control plane and dedicated cluster availability; for cross-region failover there are SLO targets and we can include operational runbooks in the contract. we'll surface the exact SLA numbers in the amendment.
09:35 Priya: thanks, this felt productive.
09:40 Lena: great, recap of next steps: 1) lena send pricing + amendment by feb 5; 2) jordan run perf bench week of feb 9; 3) mark provide traffic by feb 6; 4) security pack + kms docs to be shared.
09:58 Rajiv: i'll also prepare a short eval prompt set we want you to run during the benchmark.
10:05 Lena: thanks. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark plan.
10:12 Maya: i'll open a customer success ticket and attach security artifacts.
10:20 Aisha: procurement will expect the redlined amendment in word.
10:25 Lena: noted. thanks everyone, chat soon.

End of transcript.
